answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using capacity-bounded trust graphs with slashable collateral. When coordinating decentralized trade of raw marble, each agent routes credit along an authenticated transaction thread while pruning any circular echo of endorsements. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of locking liquid capital to expand capacity across forged nodes. However, this model centralizes routing power among wealthy incumbents and restricts bootstrapping for new agents.
